newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish sharply lower.

text.p: French stocks finished sharply lower on Wednesday as investors took profits on the market's gains ahead of the publication of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book and upcoming U.S. producer price data.

Brokers said the market came under late pressure from weaker bond prices and an early fall on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 44.45 points, or 1.65 percent, at 2,641. Volume was around nine billion francs.
Shares in Banque Nationale de Paris fell 5.74 percent to 243 francs on rumours that Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP), now part of Axa-UAP, may sell its BNP stake.
Shares in chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc fell 5.22 percent to 190.50 francs, pressured by Hoechst's forecast for lower sales in 1997.
Lafarge's stock rose 1.22 percent to 372 francs after reporting a rise in 1996 operating profit and forecasting higher 1997 profit.

Alcatel Alsthom shares closed down 3.13 percent at 620 francs after the defence ministry's announcement that state-owned Aerospatiale was barred from joining its bid for Thomson-CSF. After the close, Alcatel announced that it would bid jointly for Thomson-CSF with Dassault, a manufacturer of fighter planes.
